cases.existing_use: Limited Restaurant, about 1,900 sq ft at ground level, most recently d.b.a. Schilling & Co. (motion p. 1). The record description calls it 'an existing restaurant', which is not the Planning Code use.

triggers.what: Adding a Type 41 on-sale beer and wine licence turns the existing Limited Restaurant into a Restaurant (a change of use under § 102). At filing Table 810 made a Restaurant conditional on every story of the CCB district, including the first.
code_sections_at_filing: 810 Table (Restaurant row, 1st story C(1)(3); Notes 1 and 3)

Ord. 249-23 p. 94 shows the 1st-story "C(1)(3)" struck and replaced by "P(3)". § 102 (mirror, today's text): Restaurant, Limited "shall not provide on-site beer and/or wine sales for consumption on the premises".

Project description: "convert approximately 1,900 square feet of ground level space, most recently used as a Limited Restaurant (DBA Schilling & Co.), into Restaurant (DBA Sisterita). The change of use will permit on-sale beer and wine".
triggers.change_detail: Ord. 249-23 (File No. 230701, Citywide Expansion of Allowable Commercial, Restaurant, and Retail Uses), App. 12/14/2023, Eff. 1/14/2024: Table 810 Restaurant, 1st story, C(1)(3) to P(3); 2nd and 3rd+ stay C(1)(3). No amendment to § 810 between Ord. 190-22 (Eff. 10/17/2022) and 1/14/2024, so C applied on the 2022-12-06 filing date. Today (gocodebook.com mirror, 2026-08 edition, text as of 2026-09-23): Restaurant 'P(3) | C(1)(3) | C(1)(3)'.

filing date before 2024-01-14
proposed use is a Restaurant (on-site beer and wine, ABC Type 41)
existing lawful use is a Limited Restaurant, not an already authorised Restaurant
story (today: P on the 1st, C above; at filing C on all)
not Formula Retail (NP in Chinatown mixed use districts)
use size about 1,900 sq ft (rules out a separate use-size trigger)

notes.what_this_is: Trigger inventory for the 40 backtest cases (15 that did not reach approval (withdrawn or cancelled), 25 decided): for each case, what in the Planning Code required the Conditional Use at the filing date, whether that control has changed since, and which facts a rule needs. Built from two independent readings per case (a first reader with quotes and a blind second reader), settled by an adjudicator where they differed.
notes.how_settled: Where the two readings differed on trigger families, on the control at filing, or on whether the code changed, the difference is described in each case's 'settlement'. Most differences were labels: one reader listed a control with 'principal' to show it was checked, or the readers chose different family names for the same section. Points re-checked by the adjudicator against the cached motion or code text are marked as such in the text (D03 no § 121.2 in the motion; D20 § 178 only in the basis-for-approval sentence; D12 finding 7.D; § 202.11(d)(3), the § 102 Historic Building definition and the 'Uses in Historic Buildings' rows of Tables 715, 719 and 722; the Type 90 exclusion from the Bar definition in Ord. 249-23).

vocabulary.basis: stated_in_record = the motion or the record names this ground; inferred_from_code = the readers derived it from the code and the facts, no decision document names it; applicant_claim_only = the applicant's theory, which Planning did not adopt (N13).
vocabulary.changed_since_filing: yes = the governing text or a parameter relevant to this trigger changed after the filing date; text_only = renumbering or rewording with the same control; no = unchanged.
vocabulary.permission_changed_since_filing: Derived: yes when control_at_filing and control_today differ; depends_on_historic_building_status when the table cell is unchanged but § 202.11 (Eff. 4/11/2026) may make a C use P in a Historic Building; no otherwise. 'changed_since_filing: yes' with 'permission_changed: no' means a parameter moved (a cap, a one-square-foot threshold shift) while the permission stayed the same.
vocabulary.facts_in_concept_text: Whether the project description on the Planning record, plus what follows from the address, states the facts the rule needs: all, some or none.
vocabulary.families: new_use_control = the district's own zoning table makes the new use conditional. new_use_control_special_district = a special use district makes the use itself conditional although (or independently of whether) the base table does: § 249.60(f)(1) Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD for Restaurants, § 249.40A / § 249.38 SoMa Youth and Family SUD. laundromat_removal (§ 202.12), legacy_business_replacement (§ 754(c)(4)) and unscreened_open_air_use_waterfront_sud (§ 240.2(d)) were filed by the readers under 'other' and are named here as their own families.

notes.counting_rules: A case is counted once per family even when it has two entries in it (first and second story; baseline and sub-rule). Several cases have one real cause written in two places in the code (Table 754 or 763 plus § 249.60(f)(1); § 249.62 plus Table 737 Note 7; § 303(e) plus § 178(c)(1)): count hearings by cause once.
